literal: The trivial matter of an unlearned man's anger, at all times, him who does not yield to it, will not join, glory.
translation: Glory will never abide with one who does not know how to yield to and defuse even the trivial anger of an unlearned man.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவன் கோபப்படும் எளிய விஷயத்தைக்கூடத் தவிர்த்துக்கொள்ள உடன்படாதவனிடம், அவனது புகழானது எப்போதும் நிலைத்து நிற்காது.
explanation: This couplet explains that the anger of an unlearned or ignorant person is a trivial matter ('சிறுபொருள்'). However, a wise leader must know how to handle or yield ('ஒல்லுதல்') to such situations to avoid unnecessary conflict. If a person is stubborn and does not yield to or defuse even such minor provocations, their glory ('ஒளி') will depart from them forever ('எஞ்ஞான்றும் ஒல்லாது'). True greatness lies in knowing when to overlook the petty anger of the ignorant.
